basis: Inherited epidermal fragility with blistering and erosions; muscle, kidney and hearing involvement belongs to uncommon subtypes.
Impaired sound conduction through the external or middle ear.
Benign inflammatory depapillation of the tongue; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Colitis/parotitis, chronic otitis media and arthritis each occur in 1/2 patients; hepatosplenomegaly and glycogen accumulation alone do not establish functional injury.
Neurodevelopmental disability defines the spectrum; absent or hypoplastic nails and gingival enlargement are common defining features.
Degeneration of spinal articular cartilage and adjacent bone; neurologic compression is not inherent across patients.
Structural skeletal myopathy; respiratory insufficiency and dysphagia reflect muscle weakness rather than direct pulmonary or gastrointestinal disease.
Inherited hypoplasia of dental enamel; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Benign eccrine duct tumour arising in vulvar dermis; its tissue of origin is skin.
Complex spastic paraplegia and motor neuropathy within the P5CS-deficiency metabolic spectrum; cataracts and hearing impairment are occasional (<30%).
Malignant mature B-cell proliferation; lymphoma requires both haematologic and infectious_immune axes. No specific extranodal site is consistently affected.
Menstrual-phase-dependent fever without established immune disease or lasting injury to an axis organ; cortisol elevation is occasional.
Intellectual disability and marfanoid skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; cardiac and ocular disease are occasional (<30%).
Malabsorption and global developmental delay each occur in 3/3; cardiac defects in 1/3 omitted by cap. Wasting alone does not establish a primary metabolic disorder.
Congenital left-sided cardiac and aortic obstructive abnormalities define Shone complex.
USP18 interferonopathy with cerebral injury; respiratory failure in 4/4 with ARDS reported, thrombocytopenia in 3/5; patent ductus in 2/5 omitted by cap.
Serrated intestinal polyposis defines the disorder; cancer susceptibility does not establish damage to additional organs.
Inherited cardiac electrical dysfunction causing prolonged repolarization and ventricular arrhythmia susceptibility.
Thoracic vertebral closure defect with herniation of spinal cord and meninges; neurogenic bladder is a separately diagnosed complication.
ITK immunodeficiency with lymphoproliferation and cytopenias; effusions and hepatomegaly do not establish direct organ injury; associated lymphomas are separate diagnoses.
CACNA1C-related Brugada syndrome is a cardiac conduction and rhythm disorder.
Sensory/autonomic nerve loss; fractures (3/3), dental injury and skin wounds follow unperceived trauma. Separately diagnosed arthropathy does not add an axis.
Leucine catabolism defect; cerebral white-matter abnormalities in 4/6 and developmental delay in 30-79% support neurologic injury; optic atrophy only 1/10.
Overlap syndrome characterized by eyelid malformation, intellectual disability and patellar/skeletal abnormalities; no supplied frequency evidence supports additional axes.
Lysosomal transport disorder umbrella; renal injury in cystinosis and neurologic injury in free sialic acid storage disease are subtype-dependent, not shared across the group.
